newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan consortium wins China financial system order.
newsitem.headline: Japan consortium wins China financial system order.

text.p: A Japanese-led consortium said on Thursday that it had won an order from the People's Bank of China for a financial settlement system that it expects will become the core of financial modernisation in the nation.

The consortium, comprising Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), Hitachi Ltd, NTT Data Communications System Corp, Itochu Corp and Marubeni Corp as well as the Chinese Academy of Science, said it won the order for an automated payment system.

"An agreement for the order was officially concluded today between NTT Data and the People's Bank of China together with the China National Instruments Import and Export Corp at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing," the Japanese consortium members said in a statement on Thursday.
The statement did not say what the order was worth.
The system will use both satellite and ground networks to link 100 branches of the People's Bank of China and 500 branches of five commercial banks, the statement said.

The People's Bank of China has outlined a rough schedule to start in the first half of 1997 to build a pilot system for the network, it said. The pilot system is expected to be completed within 2-1/2 years, the statement said.
The system will initially be used in 100 cities and is expected to eventually be used nationwide, it said.
The People's Bank of China has branches in more than 2,000 cities throughout China.
In the project, NTT Data would be responsible for system integration and will develop application software, in addition to overseeing the project as a whole, the statement said.
The Chinese Academy of Science will cooperate with NTT Data in developing application software, while NTT will be in charge of the communications network system, it said.
Hitachi and International Business Machines Corp (IBM) will have responsibility for the computer systems. Marubeni and Itochu will be in charge of commercial affairs and trading duties, it said.
